intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

selected_hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy bento boxes, and join locals in celebrating the fleeting beauty of sakura season. The illuminated night viewing is especially enchanting for families.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary food market with the whole family, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki egg omelets, matcha sweets, and street snacks. Vendors are welcoming to children and it offers an authentic taste of Japanese culinary culture in a vibrant, walkable setting.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations where light, sound, and movement blend seamlessly. Children and adults alike are captivated by the ever-changing environments. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience unlike anything else in the world.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a culturally enriching day trip combining the sobering and important Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum with a ferry ride to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate, encounter friendly deer roaming freely, and enjoy local oysters and momiji manju maple leaf cakes.
experiences.location: Hiroshima city and Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and freshen up after landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Kansai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Haruka Express or JR train to Kyoto Station (~75 min, ~¥1,800). Check in to your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district. Take a gentle walk through Maruyama Park itself — the iconic weeping cherry tree (Gion Shidare-zakura) is a must-see and free to enter. Stroll along Hanamikoji Street in Gion to absorb the traditional machiya townhouse atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes just a short walk from your hotel — atmospheric and free to explore. Watch for maiko (apprentice geisha) in Gion as dusk falls. Grab a simple dinner near Gion.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or skip (arrival day)
meals.lunch: Grab an ekiben (station bento box) at Kyoto Station upon arrival — budget ¥600–¥900 for a tasty, filling local bento
meals.dinner: Ippudo Ramen or Tenkaippin Ramen near Gion — hearty bowls from ¥800–¥1,100. Alternatively, pick up onigiri and side dishes from a nearby 7-Eleven or FamilyMart convenience store for under ¥500

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to the afternoon arrival and likely jet lag. Purchase an IC card (Suica or ICOCA) at Kyoto Station for easy, discounted transit throughout the trip. Late April is prime cherry blossom season — Maruyama Park may still have late-blooming varieties.

day_by_day.morning: Start with an early morning visit to Fushimi Inari Taisha (free entry) — the iconic thousands of torii gates. Arrive before 8:00 AM to beat crowds. Hike at least to the first plateau (Yotsutsuji intersection) for panoramic views of Kyoto. The full hike takes 2–3 hours but even a partial visit is rewarding for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Tofuku-ji Temple (garden entry ¥500, grounds free) — famous for its Zen garden and autumn/spring beauty. Walk back through the Higashiyama district toward your hotel, stopping at Kiyomizudera Temple (¥500 entry) for sweeping views over Kyoto and cherry blossom scenery on the hillside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion for the free Gion Corner cultural district walk. Enjoy Nishiki Market (a 10-min bus ride) for street snacks — try tamagoyaki (egg skewers), pickled vegetables, and fresh mochi. Evening stroll back through Maruyama Park, which is often lit up during cherry blossom season.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri + miso soup cup + coffee) — ¥400–¥600, or grab tamago kake gohan at a local diner for ¥500
meals.lunch: Inari sushi (kitsune-zushi) near Fushimi Inari — small stalls sell 5-piece sets for ¥300–¥500. Very budget-friendly and fitting for the location
meals.dinner: Nishiki Market street food dinner — budget ¥800–¥1,200 per person for a variety of skewers, tofu, and snacks

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant walking and some uphill paths. Fushimi Inari is free and one of Japan's most photogenic spots. Kiyomizudera is family-friendly with wide paths. Bus day pass (¥700) is cost-effective for today's route.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Arashiyama district (30-min bus or train from Gion). Walk through the famous Arashiyama Bamboo Grove (free entry) — best experienced early morning before crowds arrive. Stop at Tenryu-ji Temple garden (¥500) for beautiful pond garden scenery, often with late cherry blossoms reflected in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arashiyama riverside — rent bicycles (¥1,000–¥1,500/day) for a fun family activity along the Oi River. Visit Jojakko-ji Temple (¥500) for a quieter, moss-covered hillside experience loved by families. Cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge for photos with mountain and river backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto city center. Visit the free Shimogamo Shrine, a UNESCO World Heritage site with a forested approach path (Tadasu no Mori). Relax at Maruyama Park for a peaceful evening under any remaining cherry blossoms.

meals.breakfast: Tofu breakfast set at a local Arashiyama café (Kyoto is famous for tofu cuisine) — ¥700–¥1,000, or convenience store option for ¥400
meals.lunch: Yudofu (hot tofu) lunch set in Arashiyama — several restaurants offer budget sets from ¥1,000–¥1,500. Alternatively, grab soba noodles at a local shop for ¥800
meals.dinner: Gyukatsu Motomura or similar katsu restaurant near Gion — pork or beef cutlet set meals from ¥900–¥1,300 including rice, miso soup, and cabbage

day_by_day.notes: Saturday means Arashiyama will be busy — arrive before 8:30 AM for the bamboo grove. The bicycle rental is a great family activity and covers more ground affordably. Arashiyama is reachable by Randen tram or JR Sagano Line from Kyoto Station.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi) — a 2 km canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees (free). Walk from Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion, ¥500 entry) southward through the path, passing small shrines and cafés. Ginkaku-ji's Zen sand garden and moss garden are serene and family-friendly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Heian Jingu Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥600 for garden) — a grand vermilion shrine with a large garden that features late cherry blossoms. Nearby Okazaki area has the Kyoto Municipal Museum of Art (free permanent collection) for a cultural and indoor afternoon option. Walk through the canal-lined Okazaki Park area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining lane parallel to the Kamo River. Browse the atmospheric alley and choose a budget-friendly spot. Sit along the Kamo River banks (Kamo-gawa) for a free, quintessential Kyoto evening experience — locals picnic here in spring.

meals.breakfast: Kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) breakfast set near Gion — toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Obanzai (Kyoto-style small dishes) lunch set near Heian Jingu — many restaurants offer affordable obanzai teishoku (set meals) for ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Pontocho budget ramen or izakaya — look for set menus or standing bars; budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person. Alternatively, picnic by the Kamo River with convenience store bento and drinks for ¥600–¥800

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is one of Kyoto's most romantic and family-friendly walks during cherry blossom season. Sunday may be crowded — start early. The Kamo River picnic is a beloved local tradition and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara (45 min from Kyoto by JR Miyakoji Rapid, ~¥720 one way). Visit Nara Park (free) — home to over 1,200 freely roaming sacred deer. Children absolutely love feeding the deer shika senbei crackers (¥200/pack sold at the park). Walk to Todai-ji Temple (¥600 entry) to see the world's largest wooden building and a giant bronze Buddha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine (free outer grounds, ¥500 for inner precincts) — famous for its hundreds of stone and bronze lanterns. Stroll through the peaceful Nara forest paths connecting the major sites. Visit Isuien Garden (¥900) for a stunning traditional Japanese garden — optional but worthwhile for culture lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto by early evening. Relax near Maruyama Park. Optional: join a free walking tour of Gion district (check local listings for free community-led tours).

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel area café before departing for Nara — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi) — a Nara specialty sold in shops near Todai-ji for ¥800–¥1,200 for a set. Or try Nakatanido's famous mochi-pounding shop for a cheap snack (¥200)
meals.dinner: Back in Kyoto — Yoshinoya or Matsuya gyudon (beef rice bowl) chain restaurant near Gion for a filling budget meal at ¥500–¥700. Or ramen from a local shop for ¥800–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Nara is an essential family day trip — the deer are a highlight for children of all ages. Bring hand sanitizer after deer feeding. The JR Kansai Area Pass or individual tickets are both viable; compare costs based on your travel pattern. Nara is very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited northern Kyoto area: Daitoku-ji Temple complex (grounds free, individual sub-temples ¥400–¥500). The complex has multiple Zen sub-temples with rock gardens — quieter and more authentic than southern Kyoto. Families can enjoy the peaceful garden atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion, ¥500) — one of Japan's most iconic sights. The gold-leafed pavilion reflected in the surrounding pond is stunning and very photogenic. Nearby Ryoan-ji Temple (¥600) features the world-famous enigmatic Zen rock garden — a UNESCO World Heritage site. Both are reachable by city bus.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion area. Explore Yasaka Shrine (free entry, open 24 hours) — beautifully lit in the evening. Browse the covered Shijo shopping arcade for budget souvenirs (100-yen shops, local snacks). Try a 100-yen store (Daiso or Seria) for affordable omiyage (souvenir) shopping.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten near hotel — morning set (toast, boiled egg, coffee) for ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Shokudo (casual Japanese diner) near Kinkaku-ji — teishoku set meals with rice, soup, and main dish for ¥800–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Izakaya near Gion — order a few shared small plates (yakitori, edamame, karaage) for ¥800–¥1,500 per person. Look for lunchtime-style early bird sets if dining before 18:00

day_by_day.notes: Kinkaku-ji is extremely popular — arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to avoid the largest crowds. The bus day pass (¥700) is excellent value for today's route covering northern and central Kyoto. Yasaka Shrine is free and magical at night.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Osaka (15 min by Hankyu or Keihan train from Kyoto, ~¥400–¥560). Visit Osaka Castle (castle tower ¥600, surrounding park free) — the park is a major cherry blossom spot and culturally significant. The castle museum inside is family-friendly with interactive exhibits about Japanese history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori district — Osaka's famous entertainment and food street. Walk along the Dotonbori canal, see the iconic Glico Running Man sign, and explore the vibrant street food scene. Visit Kuromon Ichiba Market (Osaka's kitchen) for fresh food stalls and local snacks. Browse the free Amerikamura (American Village) area for youth culture.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Osaka's legendary food culture (kuidaore — eating until you drop) in Dotonbori. Return to Kyoto by 21:00–22:00 via train.

meals.breakfast: Quick convenience store meal before departing — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Osaka street food in Dotonbori: takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥500–¥600 for 8 pieces), okonomiyaki (savory pancake, ¥700–¥1,000), or kushikatsu (fried skewers from ¥100 each). Budget ¥800–¥1,200 for a satisfying street food lunch
meals.dinner: Ichiran or Ippudo ramen in Osaka (¥890–¥1,100) — Ichiran's single-booth ramen experience is unique and budget-friendly. Or try a standing sushi bar in Namba for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is a must-visit for food lovers and families. Dotonbori is free to explore and endlessly entertaining. The Hankyu or Keihan train is cheaper than the Shinkansen for Kyoto-Osaka travel. Keep IC card topped up for seamless transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit any favorite Kyoto spots or explore areas not yet visited. Suggested: Fushimi Sake District (Fushimi-Momoyama) — walk along the historic sake brewery canal streets (Horikawa-dori area). Many breweries offer free tastings or cheap sake cups (¥100–¥300). The area is atmospheric and less touristy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Toji Temple (grounds free, treasure hall ¥500) — home to Japan's tallest pagoda (57m). The monthly flea market (Kobo-san market, held on the 21st — check if applicable) is one of Kyoto's best for antiques, crafts, and street food. Alternatively, explore the Kyoto Railway Museum (¥1,200 adults, ¥500 children) — excellent for families with kids who love trains, featuring real vintage locomotives.
day_by_day.evening: Final big Kyoto evening: walk the entire Higashiyama district from Kiyomizudera down through Ninenzaka, Sannenzaka, and into Gion at dusk. The lantern-lit streets are magical. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at budget shops along the route.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery — melon pan, coffee, and onigiri for ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Fushimi area: try a sake-lees (sake kasu) ramen or simple noodle shop — ¥700–¥1,000. Many local spots near the sake district are authentic and inexpensive
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a kaiseki-lite (simplified traditional Kyoto cuisine) set at a mid-range restaurant — look for lunch-price dinner sets or early bird specials at ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person for a memorable final Kyoto dinner

day_by_day.notes: This is a flexible day to revisit favorites or fill in gaps. The Kyoto Railway Museum is particularly great for families with younger children. Fushimi sake district is a hidden gem — quieter than central Kyoto tourist spots.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Kyoto accommodation and travel to Tokyo via Shinkansen (Nozomi/Hikari, ~2h15m, ~¥13,500 with JR Pass or standard fare). Arrive in Tokyo by late morning. Check in to budget accommodation in Tokyo (pre-booked capsule hotel or guesthouse in Asakusa or Shinjuku area — ¥3,000–¥5,000/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Asakusa district (if staying nearby) — visit Senso-ji Temple (free entry), Tokyo's oldest and most famous temple. Walk through Nakamise Shopping Street for budget souvenirs (ningyo-yaki cakes, kaminari okoshi rice crackers). Stroll along the Sumida River where cherry blossom trees may still be in late bloom.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) for an evening of free browsing through multi-story electronics and anime/manga shops — a unique cultural experience for all ages. Alternatively, visit Ueno Park (free) for a relaxed evening stroll — the park may still have late cherry blossoms.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast in Kyoto before departure — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Ekiben (train bento) purchased at Kyoto Station before boarding the Shinkansen — ¥900–¥1,200 for regional specialties. A classic Japanese travel tradition
meals.dinner: Asakusa area: Kaminarimon-dori has affordable ramen, tempura, and soba restaurants. Try Sometaro for budget okonomiyaki (¥1,000–¥1,400) or find a standing soba shop for ¥600–¥800

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance for the best availability. If you have a JR Pass, this leg is fully covered. Asakusa is one of Tokyo's most atmospheric neighborhoods and very family-friendly. Tokyo IC card (Suica) works seamlessly across all Tokyo transit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ueno Zoo (¥600 adults, ¥200 children) — Japan's oldest zoo, great for families with giant pandas and diverse wildlife. Alternatively, explore the free Tokyo National Museum exterior and gardens in Ueno Park, or visit the National Museum of Nature and Science (¥630). Ueno Park itself is free and beautiful in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Harajuku and Takeshita Street (free to browse) — Tokyo's famous youth fashion street, colorful and entertaining for all ages. Walk through Yoyogi Park (free) — a beloved Tokyo green space perfect for a relaxing picnic. Stroll along Omotesando boulevard for window shopping and people-watching (free). Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine (free) — a peaceful forested shrine in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Tokyo. Visit Shibuya Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian crossing, free and thrilling to experience. Watch from above at the free Shibuya Sky observation deck alternative: Starbucks Shibuya Tsutaya offers free views of the crossing. Reflect on the trip and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Tokyo guesthouse breakfast if included, or convenience store — ¥400–¥600. Try a tamago sando (egg sandwich) from 7-Eleven — a Tokyo classic
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepes on Takeshita Street (¥500–¥700) — a fun, affordable, and iconic Tokyo street food experience for families. Or grab a bento from a depachika (department store basement food hall) for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shibuya area: Genki Sushi (conveyor belt sushi) — plates from ¥110–¥330 each, budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person for a filling and fun final dinner. Or try Ichiran Ramen in Shibuya for a solo-booth ramen experience at ¥890–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Final day — keep luggage at the hotel or use coin lockers at a nearby station (¥300–¥600) for a hands-free last day. Confirm departure logistics: Narita Express (N'EX) or Limousine Bus to airport. Spend remaining yen on snacks and last souvenirs. Conveyor belt sushi is a perfect, fun, budget-friendly final meal for families.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Haruka Express from Kansai Airport or Shinkansen from the arrival airport to Kyoto Station (~75 min). Check in to your Boutique Stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Gion Orientation Walk — After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the historic Gion district. Wander along Hanamikoji Street, peek down Pontocho Alley, and cross the iconic Shijo Bridge over the Kamo River. This low-key introduction lets you shake off jet lag while soaking in Kyoto's atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Evening Illumination) — Head to your doorstep attraction: Maruyama Park's legendary weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura), beautifully lit up after dusk. Grab a picnic mat, pick up street snacks from nearby stalls, and enjoy the magical yozakura (night cherry blossom) experience with other families and locals.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal or airport snack on arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bento box or ramen at Kyoto Station's Porta underground food hall (~¥900–¥1,200) before heading to the hotel
meals.dinner: Omen Noodles on Shirakawa-dori — a beloved local noodle restaurant near Gion serving hearty udon sets. Family-friendly, budget ~¥1,500–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: April 15 is prime cherry blossom season in Kyoto — Maruyama Park will be stunning. The park stays open for evening illuminations until around 23:00. Keep the afternoon light to recover from travel. Pick up an IC card (Suica/ICOCA) at Kyoto Station for easy transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Daytime Hanami) — Start the day with a proper morning hanami picnic right outside your hotel. Arrive early (~8:00) before crowds swell. Spread a picnic mat under the iconic weeping cherry tree, enjoy the blossoms in morning light, and let kids explore the park's open lawns and stone bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kiyomizudera Temple & Higashiyama Stroll — Walk or take a short bus ride to the iconic Kiyomizudera Temple perched on the hillside. The approach through Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes is lined with souvenir shops, matcha ice cream stalls, and pottery boutiques — perfect for families. The temple's wooden stage offers sweeping views of Kyoto.
day_by_day.evening: Nishiki Market Evening Browse & Gion Dinner — Visit Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') before it closes (~18:00) to sample pickles, grilled skewers, and tofu donuts. Then return to Gion for a relaxed dinner at a mid-range kaiseki-lite restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Konbini picnic supplies (onigiri, tamagoyaki, juice) from a nearby 7-Eleven or FamilyMart — easy and fun for kids, ~¥600–¥800 per person
meals.lunch: Tofu cuisine lunch set at Tousuiro near Maruyama Park — Kyoto-style healthy tofu dishes, family portions available, ~¥1,800–¥2,500 per person
meals.dinner: Gion Kappa — a friendly neighborhood izakaya near Shijo-Gion with grilled yakitori, karaage, and kid-friendly options. Budget ~¥2,000–¥2,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Higashiyama involves cobblestone lanes and temple steps. Kiyomizudera entry fee: ¥500 per adult, free for children under 6. The temple is especially beautiful with cherry blossoms in bloom on the surrounding hillside.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — Take the Sagano Line from Kyoto Station to Saga-Arashiyama Station (~25 min). Arrive early (by 8:30) to beat the crowds in the iconic bamboo grove. The towering green stalks create an otherworldly tunnel — magical for kids and adults alike. Walk through at a leisurely pace and continue to Tenryuji Temple's stunning garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Iwatayama Monkey Park — From Arashiyama, hike the gentle 20-minute trail up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids can hand-feed monkeys from inside a mesh enclosure while the monkeys roam outside — a unique and hilarious reversal! Panoramic views of Kyoto from the summit are a bonus.
day_by_day.evening: Togetsukyō Bridge Sunset & Return to Gion — Stroll back across the iconic Togetsukyō Bridge over the Oi River as the sun sets behind the mountains — often with cherry blossoms framing the scene. Return to Kyoto by train and enjoy a relaxed evening in Gion.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café in Gion before departing (~8:00)
meals.lunch: Yoshida-ya near Arashiyama — a charming riverside restaurant serving soba noodles and tempura sets with mountain views. ~¥1,500–¥2,000 per person
meals.dinner: Ramen Sanjusangendo near Gion — rich tonkotsu or miso ramen, family-friendly, quick and satisfying after a full day. ~¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Monkey Park entry: ¥550 adults, ¥250 children. Tenryuji Temple garden entry: ¥500. Bring water for the monkey park hike — it's easy but uphill. Saturday will be busy; arriving at Arashiyama before 9:00 makes a significant difference. Rent a rickshaw for a fun family experience (~¥4,000–¥8,000 for 20 min).

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha — Take the JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Inari Station (5 min). Explore the world-famous vermillion torii gate tunnels of Fushimi Inari. Hike as far as the family is comfortable — even the first 30 minutes through the lower gates is spectacular. Early morning light filtering through the gates is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Philosopher's Path & Nanzenji Temple — Head north to the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi), a 2km canal-side walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees. This is one of Kyoto's finest hanami walks. End at the grand Nanzenji Temple with its towering sanmon gate and peaceful aqueduct — kids love running through the ancient brick waterway.
day_by_day.evening: Heian Shrine Torii Gate & Evening Walk — Visit the massive vermillion Heian Shrine torii gate nearby, then enjoy a calm evening stroll back toward Gion via the Okazaki canal area, often still lit with cherry blossom lanterns in mid-April.

meals.breakfast: Inari-sushi (fox sushi) from a stall near Fushimi Inari Station — a local specialty and perfect on-the-go breakfast, ~¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Omen Okazaki branch near Philosopher's Path — fresh vegetable udon in a cozy setting, ~¥1,400–¥1,800 per person
meals.dinner: Gion Hatanaka area — try Mishima-tei, a classic Kyoto sukiyaki restaurant for a special family dinner. ~¥3,500–¥5,000 per person (splurge option) or Kushi Kura yakitori for ~¥2,000

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours. Sunday will be crowded — aim to arrive by 8:00. The Philosopher's Path is at its peak beauty in mid-April. Wear layers as mornings can be cool (~12–16°C in April). Nanzenji entry to main grounds is free; inner buildings ~¥500.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum & A-Bomb Dome — Take the Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (~1 hr, ~¥5,800 on JR Pass). Visit the deeply moving Peace Memorial Museum (entry ¥200) and walk around the A-Bomb Dome and Peace Memorial Park. This is a profoundly important cultural experience — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island & Floating Torii Gate — From Hiroshima, take a 25-min ferry to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine (best at high tide). Explore the island's free-roaming deer, climb the shrine's covered walkways, and enjoy the scenic beauty. Allow 2.5–3 hours on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto — Take the ferry back to Hiroshima and Shinkansen to Kyoto (~17:30–19:00 arrival). Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick café stop in Gion before the early Shinkansen (~7:30 departure recommended)
meals.lunch: Miyajima oysters and momiji manju (maple leaf cakes) from island stalls — a must-try local specialty. Budget ~¥1,200–¥1,800 per person
meals.dinner: Izuju Sushi near Gion — a Kyoto institution serving pressed sushi (oshizushi) in a calm setting. ~¥2,000–¥2,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a long but incredibly rewarding day trip. JR Pass holders travel free on the Shinkansen and JR Ferry to Miyajima. Itsukushima Shrine entry: ¥300. Check tide times before visiting — the floating torii is most dramatic at high tide. The Peace Museum is suitable for children aged 8+ with parental guidance.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle & Kyoto Imperial Palace Park — Visit Nijo Castle (¥1,000 entry), a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 'nightingale floors' that squeak when walked on to detect intruders — kids find this fascinating. Explore the ornate painted interiors and castle gardens blooming with spring flowers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kyoto Imperial Palace Park Free Exploration — Walk to the adjacent Imperial Palace Park (free entry), a vast open green space ideal for families to relax, run, and have a picnic under cherry trees. Book an Imperial Palace interior tour in advance through the Imperial Household Agency (free, ~1 hour).
day_by_day.evening: Pontocho Alley Dinner & Kamo River Sunset — Return to Gion via the narrow lantern-lit Pontocho Alley for dinner at one of its atmospheric restaurants. Afterward, sit along the Kamo River banks where locals gather in the evenings — a quintessential Kyoto experience.

meals.breakfast: Morning set at a Kyoto kissaten (retro café) — toast, egg, and coffee in a charming old-school setting. Try Inoda Coffee near Sanjo. ~¥800–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Picnic in Imperial Palace Park — grab bento boxes from Nishiki Market or a nearby konbini. ~¥800–¥1,200 per person
meals.dinner: Pontocho Dining — Kichisen or Tagoto for mid-range kaiseki-style sets, or Yagumo for casual Japanese comfort food. ~¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle is particularly beautiful in cherry blossom season — the inner garden has late-blooming varieties. Imperial Palace tours must be booked in advance at sankan.kunaicho.go.jp (free). Tuesday tends to be less crowded than weekends. This is a gentler, more relaxed day after the Hiroshima day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Travel Day: Kyoto → Tokyo via Shinkansen — Check out of Kyoto hotel and take the Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi/Hikari to Tokyo (~2 hr 15 min). Store luggage at your Tokyo hotel and head out. Enjoy the iconic Mt. Fuji views from the right side of the train (seats D/E).
day_by_day.afternoon: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Head to the TeamLab Borderless museum (pre-book tickets online, ~¥3,200 adults / ¥1,000 children). This immersive digital art wonderland is a highlight for families — rooms of flowing light, interactive projections, and surreal installations that children and adults explore together for 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Odaiba Waterfront & Tokyo Bay Views — After TeamLab (located in Odaiba), explore the futuristic Odaiba waterfront. See the Rainbow Bridge lit up at night, visit the giant Unicorn Gundam statue outside DiverCity, and enjoy the bay views. Relaxed evening with dinner on the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Shinkansen ekiben (station bento) — pick up a beautifully packed bento at Kyoto Station before boarding. A beloved Japanese travel tradition. ~¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: TeamLab Borderless has a café inside — light meals and desserts. ~¥1,200–¥1,800. Alternatively, grab ramen near the museum.
meals.dinner: Odaiba Decks Tokyo Beach food floor — wide variety of restaurants including conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) at Sushiro, perfect for families. ~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book TeamLab Borderless tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. The new TeamLab Borderless reopened in Azabudai Hills (2024); confirm current location before visiting. Keep luggage storage in mind — most Tokyo hotels allow early luggage drop. IC cards work on all Tokyo metro and bus lines.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Head to Tsukiji Outer Market for a self-guided family food tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled egg omelette), grilled scallops, tuna sashimi, and matcha soft-serve from the market's many stalls. Arrive by 9:00 for the best selection before crowds peak. This is a hands-on, delicious cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hamarikyu Gardens & Tokyo Bay Cruise — Walk to the adjacent Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry), a beautiful traditional garden with a tidal pond and teahouse — serene amid the Tokyo skyline. Take a scenic 45-min water bus (Sumida River Cruise, ~¥1,040) up to Asakusa, passing under historic bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Asakusa & Senso-ji Temple by Night — Explore Tokyo's oldest temple, Senso-ji, as lanterns glow in the evening. Walk the Nakamise shopping street for traditional snacks and souvenirs. The Kaminarimon gate is spectacular at night. Enjoy the old-Tokyo shitamachi atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market IS breakfast — fresh sushi breakfast set at Sushi Dai or Daiwa Sushi, or graze the stalls. Budget ~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person for a satisfying market breakfast
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Hamarikyu Gardens — matcha and wagashi (Japanese sweets) set in a tranquil garden setting. ~¥800–¥1,200 per person
meals.dinner: Asakusa Imahan — a famous sukiyaki/shabu-shabu restaurant near Senso-ji with a long history. ~¥3,000–¥4,500 per person. Or Asakusa Mugitoro for affordable yam-based Japanese cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is free to explore. The inner wholesale market has moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains a food lover's paradise. The Sumida River water bus is a fun and scenic way to travel with children — check timetables at Tokyo Cruise website. Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — Visit one of Tokyo's finest parks (¥500 entry), which often has late-blooming cherry varieties in mid-to-late April. The park's blend of French formal, English landscape, and Japanese traditional gardens is beautiful. Perfect for a final hanami picnic if blossoms remain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku & Shibuya Family Exploration — Walk from Shinjuku to Harajuku. Visit the serene Meiji Jingu Shrine set in a forested park (free). Then explore Takeshita Street for crepe stalls and colorful fashion — kids love the energy. Walk down to Shibuya and experience the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing, one of the world's busiest intersections.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Tower or Shibuya Sky Observation Deck — End the day with a stunning nighttime view of Tokyo. Shibuya Sky (¥2,000 adults / ¥1,000 children, pre-book) offers a rooftop open-air experience with 360° views. Or visit the classic Tokyo Tower (¥1,200 adults / ¥700 children) for nostalgic charm.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a bakery near your hotel — Tokyo has excellent French-Japanese bakeries. Try Viron in Shibuya or a local konbini pastry spread. ~¥600–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen — pick up bento from a nearby convenience store or the park's café. ~¥800–¥1,200 per person
meals.dinner: Shibuya Hikarie or Cerulean Tower food floors — wide selection of mid-range Japanese restaurants. Try Tempura Tsunahachi (¥2,000–¥3,000) or a family-friendly ramen shop. ~¥1,800–¥2,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is a top spot for late cherry blossoms — ichiyo and kanzan varieties bloom after Somei Yoshino, so mid-April often still has color. Meiji Jingu is free and offers a peaceful forest walk. Book Shibuya Sky tickets online in advance — they sell out. This is a great day for souvenir shopping in Harajuku and Shibuya.

day_by_day.morning: Akihabara & Ueno Park Final Morning — Visit Ueno Park for a last stroll under any remaining cherry blossoms and explore the park's free outer areas. Nearby Ueno Zoo (¥600 adults / ¥200 children) is a great option for families with younger children. Then head to Akihabara for electronics, anime goods, and a retro arcade experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir Shopping & Departure Prep — Return to your hotel, collect luggage, and head to the airport. Allow 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Take the Narita Express (N'EX) from Shinjuku (~80 min, ~¥3,070) or Limousine Bus from major hotels to Haneda/Narita Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Fly home with wonderful memories of cherry blossoms, culture, and family adventures across Japan.

meals.breakfast: Final Japanese breakfast at a hotel or a traditional teishoku set at a local diner near the hotel — miso soup, grilled fish, rice, and pickles. ~¥800–¥1,200 per person
meals.lunch: Ueno Ameya-yokocho (Ameyoko) Market street food — a bustling open-air market with yakitori, fresh fruit, and cheap eats. ~¥800–¥1,500 per person
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent food options. Treat the family to a final ramen or sushi set at the airport food hall. ~¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Spend any remaining yen at Ameyoko Market or airport duty-free. Japan Post at the airport allows you to ship home any extra luggage you've accumulated. Use leftover IC card balance at airport convenience stores. Haneda Airport is closer to central Tokyo (~30 min); Narita requires more travel time (~60–90 min) — plan accordingly. Don't forget to reclaim consumption tax refunds at airport tax-free counters if you made qualifying purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Maruyama Park, Gion district, Kyoto Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Spread a picnic blanket, enjoy bento boxes, and join locals in celebrating the fleeting beauty of sakura season. The illuminated night viewing is especially enchanting for families.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Tokyo's legendary food market with the whole family, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki egg omelets, matcha sweets, and street snacks. Vendors are welcoming to children and it offers an authentic taste of Japanese culinary culture in a vibrant, walkable setting.

experiences.name: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse your family in a breathtaking world of interactive digital art installations where light, sound, and movement blend seamlessly. Children and adults alike are captivated by the ever-changing environments. A truly unique cultural and artistic experience unlike anything else in the world.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids love feeding the monkeys from inside a viewing hut while enjoying panoramic views of Kyoto below.

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial and Miyajima Island Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a culturally enriching day trip combining the sobering and important Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum with a ferry ride to Miyajima Island. See the iconic floating torii gate, encounter friendly deer roaming freely, and enjoy local oysters and momiji manju maple leaf cakes.
experiences.location: Hiroshima city and Miyajima Island, Hiroshima Prefecture

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00. Nothing scheduled before arrival. After clearing customs and immigration, arrange a pre-booked luxury airport transfer (private car or Shinkansen Green Car) from the airport to Kyoto. Settle into your boutique stay in Maruyama Park, Gion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Gion Orientation Walk — After check-in, take a leisurely stroll through the atmospheric Gion district. Admire the preserved machiya townhouses on Hanamikoji Street, spot geiko and maiko, and soak in the refined atmosphere of Japan's most iconic geisha quarter. Visit the iconic Yasaka Shrine, just steps from the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park (Night Hanami) — Experience the magical illuminated weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) in Maruyama Park, located right at your doorstep. The park's centrepiece cherry tree is dramatically lit after dark — a once-in-a-lifetime sight. Enjoy a curated bento picnic set arranged by the hotel under the blossoms.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a meal on the plane or grab a light snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a premium ekiben (luxury train bento box) from Kyoto Station upon arrival — try the Kyoto Kaiseki Bento from Shin-Shin or a Kyoto beef bento.
meals.dinner: Kikunoi Honten — A three-Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in Higashiyama, a 5-minute walk from the hotel. Seasonal tasting menus celebrate spring ingredients and cherry blossom themes. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The boutique stay in Maruyama Park places you literally at the centre of Kyoto's most celebrated cherry blossom viewing spot — no transport needed for evening hanami. Jet lag tip: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time to adjust faster. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange next-day reservations and experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Fushimi Inari Taisha & Tofukuji Temple — Start early (07:00) to beat crowds at Fushimi Inari, the mesmerising shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Hike as far as the family is comfortable (the lower trails are accessible for all ages). Afterwards, stop at nearby Tofukuji Temple, renowned for its Zen garden and cherry blossom-framed bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Nishiki Market & Teramachi Shopping Street — Head to Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for a premium guided food tasting tour. Sample Kyoto pickles (tsukemono), fresh yuba (tofu skin), grilled skewers, and seasonal sweets. Browse the elegant Teramachi covered arcade for artisan crafts and wagashi (Japanese confections) as family souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Maiko Dinner Experience — Book a private ozashiki (geisha banquet) experience through the hotel concierge. Enjoy a multi-course kaiseki dinner in a private tatami room while being entertained by a maiko performing traditional dances and playing ozashiki games with the family — a deeply authentic and exclusive Kyoto experience.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — Request a traditional Japanese morning meal (gohan, miso soup, grilled fish, pickles, tamagoyaki) served in your room or the hotel's private dining area.
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market grazing — Curated premium tastings along the market including fresh sashimi, Kyoto-style rolled sushi, and seasonal mochi.
meals.dinner: Private ozashiki kaiseki dinner at a Gion ochaya (teahouse) — arranged exclusively through the hotel concierge. Expect 10–12 courses of exquisite seasonal Kyoto cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Fushimi Inari before 07:30 for the most serene experience — it becomes very busy by mid-morning. The ozashiki experience must be booked 2–4 weeks in advance and typically requires an introduction through a trusted contact such as your luxury hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park — Take a private car or rickshaw to Arashiyama. Walk through the iconic towering bamboo grove at dawn for an ethereal atmosphere. Then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park for panoramic views over Kyoto and playful encounters with Japanese macaques — a highlight for families. Visit Tenryuji Temple's stunning garden, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sagano Romantic Train & Hozugawa River Boat Cruise — Board the scenic Sagano Romantic Train through the Hozu River gorge with its dramatic cliffs and cherry blossom-lined banks. Connect to the traditional wooden Hozugawa River Boat for a relaxing 16km downstream cruise back toward Arashiyama — a spectacular and leisurely family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Gion — Relaxed evening in the Gion and Higashiyama area. Stroll the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional shops and lanterns at dusk. Enjoy a private sake tasting and pairing session arranged by the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Western or Japanese set, taken early before departure to Arashiyama.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shoraian — A celebrated restaurant set in a historic riverside villa in Arashiyama, serving refined kaiseki cuisine with garden and river views.
meals.dinner: Mizai — A Michelin two-star restaurant in Higashiyama offering exquisite contemporary kaiseki. Alternatively, enjoy a curated in-hotel dinner with seasonal Kyoto dishes if the family prefers a quieter evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Sagano Romantic Train tickets in advance as they sell out quickly, especially on weekends in cherry blossom season. The Monkey Park hike is approximately 20 minutes uphill — comfortable shoes recommended. Private rickshaw (jinrikisha) service in Arashiyama can be hired for a luxurious and effortless way to see the area.

day_by_day.morning: Nijo Castle & Kyoto Imperial Palace — Begin with Nijo Castle, the opulent shogun's residence famous for its 'nightingale floors' (chirping floorboards designed to detect intruders) and stunning Ninomaru Palace interiors. Walk through the castle's cherry blossom garden. Then visit the Kyoto Imperial Palace and its expansive park — a peaceful green oasis in the city centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion) & Ryoanji Zen Garden — Visit the world-famous Golden Pavilion, shimmering in gold leaf on its reflective pond, surrounded by spring foliage. Continue to Ryoanji Temple for Japan's most celebrated Zen rock garden — a meditative and culturally profound experience. Explore the surrounding Kinugasa area.
day_by_day.evening: Kyoto Station Isetan Dining & Kyoto Tower Observatory — Head to Kyoto Station for dinner at one of the premium restaurants in The Cube dining complex inside Kyoto Station Isetan. Afterwards, visit the Kyoto Tower Observatory for sweeping night views over the city and its sea of cherry blossoms.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Kanga-an — A refined shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) restaurant near Ryoanji, offering a meditative and exquisite multi-course lunch experience in a historic temple setting.
meals.dinner: Wakuden in Kyoto Station — A celebrated Kyoto kaiseki restaurant inside the station building, offering beautifully presented seasonal cuisine in an elegant setting.

day_by_day.notes: Nijo Castle is best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive. Pre-book Kanga-an for lunch as it has limited seating. The Kyoto Tower Observatory is a fun, accessible activity for children in the family.

day_by_day.morning: Hiroshima Peace Memorial & Atomic Bomb Dome — Take an early Shinkansen (bullet train) Green Car from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1.5 hours). Visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum for a deeply moving and historically important experience. Walk through Peace Memorial Park and reflect at the Atomic Bomb Dome, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Miyajima Island — Itsukushima Shrine & Mt. Misen — Take the short ferry to Miyajima Island. Visit the iconic Itsukushima Shrine with its famous 'floating' torii gate rising from the sea. Encounter the friendly free-roaming deer on the island. Take the ropeway up Mt. Misen for breathtaking panoramic views over the Seto Inland Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto — Take the Shinkansen back to Kyoto. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Gion district, perhaps browsing the evening lantern-lit streets before retiring.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or a premium convenience store ekiben for the Shinkansen journey.
meals.lunch: Kakifuku — A renowned restaurant on Miyajima Island specialising in Hiroshima's famous oysters, served grilled, fried, or in a rich oyster nabe (hot pot). A premium and locally iconic lunch.
meals.dinner: Gion Nanba — A celebrated Gion restaurant offering beautifully crafted obanzai (Kyoto home-style) cuisine and seasonal dishes in an intimate, traditional setting.

day_by_day.notes: This is an emotionally significant day — the Peace Memorial Museum is profoundly moving and appropriate for older children. Allow time for quiet reflection. The floating torii gate is best seen at high tide for the iconic floating effect — check tide tables in advance. Miyajima's oysters are a must-try local delicacy.

day_by_day.morning: Philosopher's Path & Nanzenji Temple — Walk the famous Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi), a canal-side stone walkway lined with hundreds of cherry trees in full bloom — one of Japan's most beautiful spring walks. End at the grand Nanzenji Temple complex, featuring a striking Roman-style aqueduct and serene sub-temples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heian Shrine & Okazaki Cultural District — Visit the majestic Heian Shrine with its expansive garden featuring weeping cherry trees and a stunning pond landscape. Explore the Okazaki area's museums, including the Kyoto National Museum of Modern Art or the Fureaikan Kyoto Museum of Traditional Crafts for family-friendly cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Private Tea Ceremony & Kaiseki Dinner — Participate in an exclusive private tea ceremony (chado) hosted in a traditional machiya townhouse in the Higashiyama area, guided by a certified tea master. Follow with a private kaiseki dinner at the venue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Omen — A beloved Kyoto noodle restaurant near Nanzenji, famous for its thick udon served with seasonal vegetables and a rich dipping broth. Simple, authentic, and delicious.
meals.dinner: Private kaiseki dinner as part of the tea ceremony experience, or Hyotei — A legendary three-Michelin-starred restaurant in the Okazaki area, serving refined Kyoto cuisine in a beautiful historic setting (book months in advance).

day_by_day.notes: The Philosopher's Path is at its absolute peak during mid-April — timing this walk during morning light is magical and less crowded. The private tea ceremony can be arranged through the hotel concierge and typically lasts 60–90 minutes. Hyotei requires reservations many months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Nara — Take a comfortable express train to Nara (45 minutes from Kyoto). Visit Todaiji Temple, home to Japan's largest bronze Buddha (Daibutsu), an awe-inspiring sight for the whole family. Roam Nara Park and feed the famous free-roaming sacred deer — a beloved and joyful family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kasuga Taisha Shrine & Naramachi — Visit the atmospheric Kasuga Grand Shrine, with its thousands of bronze and stone lanterns lining forest paths. Explore the charming Naramachi merchant district with its preserved machiya townhouses, artisan shops, and traditional craft workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto — Evening at leisure in Gion. Optional: attend a traditional Kabuki or Noh theatre performance at the Gion Hatanaka or check listings for the Minami-za Theatre.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Yoshikasuga — A refined restaurant in Nara serving kaiseki-inspired cuisine using local Yamato ingredients, including Yamato beef and seasonal mountain vegetables, in a tranquil garden setting.
meals.dinner: Nakamura — One of Kyoto's oldest and most prestigious kaiseki restaurants (founded 1716), located in the Nishiki area, offering centuries of culinary tradition in an exquisite setting.

day_by_day.notes: Deer crackers (shika senbei) are sold throughout Nara Park for feeding the deer — a highlight for children. The deer are gentle but can be persistent! Nara is easily done as a half-day or full-day trip from Kyoto. The Minami-za Theatre in Gion is Japan's oldest kabuki theatre — check the April performance schedule in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Shinkansen to Tokyo — Check out of the Kyoto boutique stay and board the Shinkansen Nozomi (Green Car) to Tokyo (approximately 2 hours 15 minutes). Enjoy the iconic view of Mt. Fuji from the right-hand side of the train on a clear day. Check into a luxury Tokyo hotel (e.g., Aman Tokyo, The Peninsula, or Park Hyatt Tokyo).
day_by_day.afternoon: TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — Immerse the whole family in the extraordinary world of teamLab Borderless, one of Tokyo's most spectacular attractions. Wander through boundless rooms of flowing light, interactive digital art, and immersive sound installations — a breathtaking and endlessly engaging experience for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Shibuya & Omotesando — Experience the electric energy of Shibuya Crossing, the world's busiest pedestrian scramble, from a premium vantage point. Stroll the elegant Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — lined with flagship luxury boutiques and architecturally stunning buildings.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Kyoto hotel or a premium ekiben purchased at Kyoto Station for the Shinkansen journey.
meals.lunch: Lunch at teamLab Borderless venue café or nearby Odaiba dining — or head to Toyosu Market area for a premium sushi lunch.
meals.dinner: Sushi Saito (if accessible through concierge connections) or Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten — legendary three-Michelin-star sushi counter in Ginza. Alternatively, Florilège — a celebrated modern French-Japanese restaurant with two Michelin stars in Aoyama.

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless reopened in a new Azabudai Hills location — book timed-entry tickets well in advance as they sell out. Seat on the right-hand side of the Shinkansen (seats A/B) for the best Mt. Fuji views. The hotel concierge in Tokyo will be essential for securing premium restaurant reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — Explore the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market with the whole family on a guided premium food tour. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled seafood skewers, wagyu beef, fresh fruit, and artisan Japanese snacks. Visit the iconic tuna auction area (advance reservation required) at nearby Toyosu Market if arranged.
day_by_day.afternoon: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Experience — Visit Tokyo's oldest and most beloved temple, Senso-ji, in the historic Asakusa district. Walk the vibrant Nakamise shopping street for premium souvenirs. Participate in a hands-on traditional craft workshop (e.g., wagashi sweet-making, origami, or furoshiki wrapping) at a nearby cultural studio — ideal for families.
day_by_day.evening: Tokyo Skytree & Sumida River Cruise — Ascend the Tokyo Skytree (634m) to the Tembo Deck and Tembo Galleria for spectacular panoramic night views over the entire city. Board a private yakatabune (traditional wooden boat) for a lantern-lit evening cruise along the Sumida River with dinner served on board.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at the luxury Tokyo property.
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market tour grazing — Fresh sushi, uni (sea urchin), tamagoyaki, and seasonal delicacies sourced directly from market vendors.
meals.dinner: Private yakatabune dinner cruise on the Sumida River — Traditional Japanese multi-course dinner (kaiseki-style or izakaya-style) served aboard a beautifully decorated traditional wooden boat with river and city views.

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market food tour is best done early (08:00–10:00) when produce is freshest. Book the yakatabune cruise well in advance — private boats are available for exclusive family hire. The Skytree's Tembo Galleria (450m) offers a glass-floored walkway that is thrilling for adventurous family members.

day_by_day.morning: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — Visit Tokyo's most magnificent park and garden for a final morning of cherry blossom viewing. Shinjuku Gyoen blends Japanese, French, and English garden styles across 58 hectares and is home to over 1,000 cherry trees — a serene and beautiful farewell to Japan's spring season. Enjoy a picnic breakfast arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Harajuku & Meiji Shrine — Walk through the forested path to the majestic Meiji Shrine, a peaceful Shinto sanctuary dedicated to Emperor Meiji. Explore the colourful Takeshita Street in Harajuku for unique Japanese pop culture and street food. Browse the premium boutiques and concept stores of Ura-Harajuku and Cat Street.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Omakase Dinner & Departure Preparation — Enjoy a final celebratory omakase dinner at one of Tokyo's finest sushi or kaiseki establishments. Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure. Arrange a pre-booked luxury private car transfer to the airport for the outbound flight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel picnic breakfast arranged for Shinjuku Gyoen — premium onigiri, seasonal fruit, pastries, and Japanese teas presented in an elegant bento format.
meals.lunch: Harajuku Gyukatsu Motomura or a premium crepe and café lunch in the Omotesando Hills complex — a relaxed and fun family lunch.
meals.dinner: Sushi Yoshitake (three Michelin stars, Ginza) or Quintessence (three Michelin stars, Shinagawa) — a spectacular farewell dinner celebrating 10 extraordinary days in Japan. Book months in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen opens at 09:00 — arrive early for a tranquil final cherry blossom experience before the park fills. Allow sufficient time for airport transfer — Narita requires at least 2.5 hours and Haneda 1.5 hours before international departure. The hotel concierge can arrange luggage forwarding (takkyubin) to the airport the evening before for a stress-free final morning.
